cause: Reference hunting outside the workspace: the agent (mostly delegated helpers, occasionally itself) fetched code from the network or read other installed copies of the library to compare against, without stating a boundary in the helper's brief and without ever auditing the commands the helper actually ran before trusting its verdict; out-of-bounds evidence gathering disqualified the attempt even when every test passed.
rule: All evidence must come from the working tree: never fetch code from the network or read another installed copy of the library, in any thread. When you delegate, state that boundary in the brief, and before trusting a helper's verdict inspect the commands it actually ran and reject any that reached outside the working tree.
predicted_effect: Attempts whose fixes pass the tests will stop being voided: helpers will stay inside the workspace because the brief says so, and any out-of-bounds command a helper runs anyway will be caught and discounted before the attempt finishes, instead of silently invalidating correct work.
learned: I learned that correct fixes were being thrown away because evidence was gathered outside the working tree — usually by an unconstrained, never-audited helper — so every task now ends with a step that states the boundary up front and checks what helpers actually ran before trusting them.
